title: Posit Assistant: stabilize request prefix for Custom Providers relying on implicit prefix caching
description: ## Original post by @Zessi-C in https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/discussions/15054 > I'm using Positron Assistant with a Custom Provider (OpenAI-compatible endpoint) pointing to Alibaba Cloud Model Studio (Qwen 3.8 Max). This provider uses **implicit prefix caching** — the platform automatically caches KV states for byte-identical prompt prefixes, with no `cache_control` markers available in the OpenAI Chat Completions protocol. > > In practice, I'm seeing a cache hit rate of only ~60%, with very high `cache_write` tokens on every request. By comparison, tools that deliberately stabilize their prefix (e.g., Claude Code) achieve 90%+ hit rates with similar caching mechanisms. > > ### Root cause analysis > > I believe the gap comes from how Positron constructs requests for Custom Providers. Several aspects of the current request structure destabilize the prefix: > > **1. Conditional tool list (#8974)** > > The team identified this in #8974: tools like `inspectVariables`, `documentEdit`, and `selectionEdit` are added/removed based on IDE state. Since tools are serialized at the top of the request, any change invalidates the entire prefix. #8974 was closed because "Posit Assistant manages tools differently" — but for Custom Providers on OpenAI-compatible endpoints, there is no `cache_control` mechanism to mitigate this. The full cost of the cache miss is borne by the user. > > **2. Dynamic IDE context in early message positions (#9973)** > > Each request injects session state including: > - A timestamp precise to the second (`Today's date is: Wednesday, October 15, 2025 at 12:48:45 PM CDT`) > - Variable lists that change as the user runs code > - Session metadata > > While #9973 fixed the ordering (user instruction moved last), the dynamic content itself still appears within the conversation body. Any change in these blocks shifts all subsequent bytes, breaking prefix matching for everything after them. > > **3. No provider-level caching awareness (#13817)** > > Currently, all Custom Provider models are treated as generic OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions. There's no way to signal that a provider relies on implicit prefix caching and would benefit from prefix stabilization. The `promptCaching` override added for Bedrock (#12142) only controls Anthropic-style explicit caching. > > ### Measured impact > > - **Cache hit rate**: ~60% (vs. 90%+ reported by tools with stable prefixes) > - **cache_write tokens**: very high on every turn, indicating the prefix is being re-cached repeatedly > - **Context growth**: input tokens grow rapidly per turn due to accumulated tool results and IDE context > > > > > ### Proposed changes > > I'd like to suggest these as considerations for the ongoing Custom Provider work (#13817, #14467): > > 1. **Stabilize the tool list for Custom Providers**: always send the full tool set regardless of IDE state (the trade-off discussed in #8974 — slightly more input tokens per request vs. massive cache miss penalty — strongly favors a stable list when implicit caching is in play). > > 2. **Move dynamic content to the tail**: timestamps, variable snapshots, and session state should appear as late as possible in the message sequence, ideally in the final user turn. The system message and tool definitions should be byte-identical across turns. > > 3. **Reduce timestamp granularity or remove it from the cached prefix**: a date like "2026-07-22" is sufficient for most tasks; "12:48:45 PM CDT" changes every second and guarantees a prefix miss if it appears early. > > 4. **Expose a caching mode in model overrides**: something like `"prefixCaching": "implicit" | "explicit" | "none"` in the per-model config. When set to `"implicit"`, Positron would apply prefix stabilization heuristics. This follows the pattern established by the `promptCaching` boolean for Bedrock (#12142). > > ### Related issues > > - #8974 — conditional tools cause cache misses (closed; fix scoped to Posit Assistant managed service) > - #13817 — model-specific handling for Custom Provider (open; natural home for this) > - #12142 — Bedrock prompt caching broke unsupported models (fixed with per-model override) > - #9973 — user instruction ordering (fixed; revealed dynamic context structure) > - #14792 — Custom Provider receives heavy IDE context injection > > ### Environment > > - Positron Version: 2026.07.1 build 5 > - Code - OSS Version: 1.118.0 > - Commit: d3cdd608df5afa3378c24c9a9c81b01fe1433a87 > - Date: 2026-07-08T19:52:09-06:00 > - Electron: 39.8.8 > - Chromium: 142.0.7444.265 > - Node.js: 22.22.1 > - V8: 14.2.231.22-electron.0 > - OS: Darwin arm64 25.5.0 > - Custom Provider → `https://token-plan.cn-beijing.maas.aliyuncs.com/compatible-mode/v1` > - Model: Qwen 3.8 Max (implicit prefix caching, no `cache_control` support)

title: Support prompts/instructions independently of skills/commands
description:
## Original post by @randrescastaneda in https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/discussions/15059

> We (and I suspect other teams) built workflows around custom prompt files (`.github/prompts/*.prompt.md`, `.vscode/positron/prompts/`, etc.) that were previously usable as `/name` slash commands in Positron Assistant. That capability appears to no longer work — Posit Assistant does not read or expose these files as commands, and there is no setting (including `chat.promptFilesLocations`, which is a VS Code-core setting Posit Assistant doesn't consult) that restores it.
> 
> ## Why this matters
> 
> Several of us have built non-trivial systems on top of custom prompts/commands: multi-step workflows, team conventions, orchestration across agent files, shared contracts between prompts, etc. Losing native support means re-engineering these systems from scratch, which is a significant cost for teams that had already standardized around this pattern. This is especially frustrating because:
> 
> - The rest of the VS Code-adjacent ecosystem — VS Code itself (via Copilot Chat), Cursor, OpenCode, Claude Code, and Codex — all support user-defined prompt files or custom commands as a first-class, low-friction feature.
> - Positron is a VS Code fork, so users reasonably expect this class of customization to carry over or have a clear equivalent.
> 
> ## Prompts/commands are not the same as skills
> 
> We understand Posit Assistant's answer to this is "convert your prompt files into skills" (`SKILL.md`, auto-loaded by description relevance). We want to push back on that being treated as a drop-in replacement:
> 
> - **Skills are context-loading modules, not invocable workflows.** They're designed to be discovered by relevance to a task description and loaded into context — not necessarily to be deterministically triggered on demand the way a slash command is.
> - **Prompts/commands are explicit and deterministic.** When I type `/cg-brainstorm` (one of commands of [this plugin](https://github.com/GPID-WB/compound-gpid) ), I want that exact workflow to run, right now — not for the assistant to decide it's relevant based on matching my message against a description. For teams with prompt files that orchestrate multi-step processes (referencing other agent files, shared contracts, specific tool sequences), that determinism is the point.
> - **Not every prompt maps cleanly to "specialized knowledge."** Some of our prompt files are procedural scripts (e.g., "run this exact sequence of steps against this file with these guardrails") rather than domain knowledge to load. Forcing these into the skill format loses the explicit-invocation guarantee and adds migration overhead for something that used to be a plain markdown file in a folder.
> 
> ## Ask
> 
> Could Posit Assistant add native support for user-defined prompt/command files (e.g., recognizing `.github/prompts/*.prompt.md`, or a Positron-specific equivalent), independent of the skills system? At minimum, it would help to have:
> 
> 1. A documented, first-class way to register custom slash commands from markdown files (not routed through skill discovery).
> 2. Compatibility with (or an explicit statement about) `chat.promptFilesLocations` and related VS Code chat settings, since those are the conventions many of us already have in place.
> 3. Clarity in the docs on the intended distinction between "skills" and "commands/prompts," since right now the skills docs read as if they're meant to cover this use case, but in practice they don't behave the same way.
> 
> Happy to share examples of the workflows this would unblock if useful.
> 
> Thank you so much!!

title: Feature request: search conversation history
description:
The conversation token counter and compaction features make it easy to manage context and cost — conversations can be pruned and renamed to keep them focused. Over time this naturally leads to a larger collection of shorter, well-titled conversations.

The problem is rediscoverability. A renamed conversation captures the general topic but not the specific terms discussed. For example, I might remember asking about `mirai_map` vs `in_parallel`, but have no way to locate which conversation that was without opening each one. A simple full-text search across conversation history — either titles or message content — would solve this directly.

**Proposed behaviour:**

A search box in the conversation history panel (or accessible via command palette)
Matches against conversation titles and/or message content
Results navigate to the matching conversation
This feels like a natural companion to the existing history, branching, and export features.

title: Improve edit tool diff and approval UX
description:
## Summary

The current approval flow for the edit tool makes it awkward to review and adjust larger or multi-hunk edits. It works fine for small, single-purpose changes and for users who approve without inspecting, but it does not scale well when the user agrees with most of a proposed edit and wants to tweak a small part of it.

## Background

Follow-up from posit-dev/positron#14755. The chat-first, agentic direction of Posit Assistant is a welcome shift, but the code editing experience currently trails what Positron Assistant and Copilot Chat offered. In particular, the edit tool routinely proposes approvals that touch many lines, presented as a single unified diff block.

When a reviewer agrees with most of the proposal but wants to alter one part of it, the practical options today are:

1. Accept the whole edit, then send a follow-up message asking for a correction.
2. Decline with instructions describing the desired tweak, and hope the retry changes only that piece.
3. Accept the whole edit and then manually adjust the file in the editor.

All three paths are token-heavy and slow. Options 1 and 2 can churn portions of the file that were already correct, forcing another full review. Option 3 avoids the retry but leaves the agent unaware of the user's change; its next turn typically starts with a read to reconcile state, adding a round-trip that the tool could have avoided by conveying user modifications directly in its response. In practice all of this discourages careful review, which is exactly the opposite of what people early on the AI adoption curve need.

## What "good" could look like

- A reviewer can accept part of a proposed edit and reject or modify the rest, without re-running the tool.
- A reviewer can adjust the exact text that will be applied inside the approval flow, so small tweaks do not require another model round-trip.
- Feedback on a rejected portion can be scoped so the retry does not disturb parts the user already accepted.
- When a reviewer modifies the applied text, the resulting change is reflected in the edit tool's response so the agent knows exactly what was applied and does not need to rediscover it with a follow-up read call.
- The review flow stays inside the chat window and tool UI, consistent with Posit Assistant's chat-first direction.
- Users who prefer the current one-click flow, or who run with edit pre-approved, are not slowed down.

title: Support Installing Claude Code Marketplace Skills/Plugins Directly from Posit Assistant
description:
@Hi folks! We'd love if Posit Assistant could support installing Claude Code marketplace skills/plugins directly, similar to Claude Code's `/plugin` workflow.
Currently, the only [supported path](https://assistant.posit.co/docs/features/skills/) is to manually copy/clone the skill into `.posit/assistant/skills/ `(or use `/import-instructions`, which effectively does the same thing). This works, but creates a separate local copy of the skill.

description:

#### Positron and OS details:

OS: Apple M3 Pro, Tahoe 26.5.1

#### Session details:

- Language runtime: R 4.5.2
- Positron Assistant model: `Claude Opus 4.8` (GitHub Copilot provider)
- GitHub Copilot organization has **vision/image input disabled** by policy.

## Describe the issue:

When Positron Assistant runs code that produces a plot (via the `executeCode` tool), the tool result is returned to the model as an `image/png` part so the model can "see" the plot. That image is then retained in the conversation history and re-sent to the model on **every** subsequent turn.

My GitHub Copilot organization does not allow vision/image input. As a result, the very next request fails with:

```
[An error occurred: Request Failed: 400 {"error":{"message":"vision is not enabled for this organization","code":""}}]
```

The real problem is not that the assistant attempted to use the tool — it's that **the conversation becomes permanently stuck**. Because the image part stays in the message history, every following request re-sends it and gets the same `400` back. There is no way to continue the conversation; each new message just repeats the identical error.

In my session this happened after the assistant generated a plot during code execution. I even told it explicitly "don't use vision to assess your work, I don't have vision enabled," but the next turn still errored, and a later unrelated request ("just add the results to my `.qmd` file") failed with the same `400` because the image was still in the history.

I don't mind that Positron Assistant tries to use vision/the plot the first time. But when the provider rejects vision content, the assistant should degrade gracefully (e.g. strip image parts from the outgoing request, or fall back to a text-only payload) so the chat can continue, rather than getting trapped in a repeating error.

## Steps to reproduce the issue:

1. Use Positron Assistant with the GitHub Copilot provider, signed in to an organization that has **vision/image input disabled**.
2. Ask the assistant to run R (or Python) code that produces a plot, so the `executeCode` tool result includes an `image/png` part (the generated plot).
3. Send any follow-up message in the same conversation.

Each follow-up request now includes the image from the earlier tool result and fails with `400 vision is not enabled for this organization`. The conversation cannot be continued.

## Expected or desired behavior:

- When the selected provider/organization does not support vision, Positron Assistant should not send image parts to the model. It should strip or omit image content (plots, screenshots, image tool results) from the request payload and fall back to a text-only message.
- Hitting the `vision is not enabled for this organization` error once should not poison the rest of the conversation. The user should be able to keep chatting after the error instead of getting the same `400` on every subsequent turn.
- Ideally, detect the org/provider vision capability up front and avoid attaching plot images (or surface a one-time, non-blocking notice) rather than failing the request.

## Were there any error messages in the UI, Output panel, or Developer Tools console?

Yes. The assistant response area showed (repeatedly, on every subsequent turn):

```
[An error occurred: Request Failed: 400 {"error":{"message":"vision is not enabled for this organization","code":""}}]
```

Context from the conversation transcript:
- An earlier `executeCode` tool result (`toolName: executeCode`) returned both a text result (`[plot generated]`) and an `image/png` part (~96 KB base64 plot).
- From that point on, every assistant turn returned the `400 vision is not enabled for this organization` error, including turns where I asked for something unrelated to the plot.

title: Assistant: Allow users to configure context window / max input tokens
description:
## Summary

Posit Assistant's compaction and truncation policy is currently anchored entirely on the value reported by the model itself. I'd like a user-configurable `model.contextLength` field (or similarly named) so the client-side budget can be set explicitly.

This is **not** about expanding the model's real window — that is and should remain a model-side property. It is about letting the user tell the client **what number to plan around** for compaction, micro-compaction, and "context remaining" indicators.

## Why this is useful

1. **Conservative budgeting.** On a long-running session with a 128k model, I'd like the client to behave as if the window is 80k so that compaction triggers earlier and a single large tool result doesn't blow the budget unexpectedly.
2. **Custom providers via `openai-compatible`.** When routing through a proxy or self-hosted gateway, the model-reported window may be wrong or unknown; a user override handles this cleanly.
3. **Cost / cache control.** Smaller effective windows keep the prompt cache leaner on metered providers.
4. **Consistency with peers.** Aider, Continue.dev, Cline, OpenCode, Roo Code, etc. all expose a `contextLength` / `maxInputTokens` / `--max-context` knob for this. Posit Assistant already exposes part of the policy (`features.autoCompactTokenBuffer`, `features.microCompactTokenThreshold`), but the underlying budget is locked.

## Proposed behavior

A new field, e.g. `model.contextLength` (integer, tokens):

```json
{
  "model": {
    "id": "MiniMax-M3",
    "provider": "openai-compatible",
    "contextLength": 80000
  }
}
```

Semantics:
- Default: whatever the model / provider reports (current behavior, no change).
- When set, used for: auto-compaction trigger, micro-compaction threshold, "context remaining" UI.
- Does **not** change what the model can accept. Setting it larger than the real window will still cause API-level failures.

## Related

- posit-dev/positron#9883 already uses the "max input tokens" term internally in a different context — exposing it as a user-configurable setting would close a gap.
- `features.autoCompactTokenBuffer` and `features.microCompactTokenThreshold` exist as partial controls; `model.contextLength` would set the underlying budget they reference.

## Environment

- Posit Assistant 0.6.0
- Positron 2026.06.0
- Provider: openai-compatible (`api.minimaxi.com/v1`)
- Model: MiniMax-M3 (128k)

The built-in commands that appear in the autocomplete menu (like /plan, /clean, /report, etc.) are hardcoded into the product itself, not user-creatable. There is currently no way to register a custom skill as a slash command that shows up in the autocomplete UI.

The skill wouldn't surface in the autocomplete dropdown the way built-in commands do.

Your options for easier invocation:

Type a short natural-language phrase that matches the skill's description, e.g. "reformat and flatten the current file" — the skill should auto-activate from that.
Keep typing /reformat and rely on the fact that the skill instructions are loaded once the assistant interprets the intent.

compatibility: Designed for Posit Assistant in Positron. Operates on the active open file.
---

# Reformat and Flatten File

Reformat the **entire content** of the active file by applying the three rules below. Read the file first, apply all transformations, then write it back.

## Rules

### Rule 1 — Assignment operator (`<-`)

If a `<-` is followed by any non-whitespace content on the **same line**, insert a newline immediately after the `<-` (preserving any leading indentation of the value that follows).

**Before:**
```r
result <- some_function(arg1, arg2)
x <- 42
```

**After:**
```r
result <-
  some_function(arg1, arg2)
x <-
  42
```

### Rule 2 — Parentheses (`(` and `)`)

- Insert a newline **after** every unescaped `(`.
- Insert a newline **before** every unescaped `)`.

"Unescaped" means not preceded by `\` (i.e., not a literal `\(` or `\)` inside a string or regex).

**Before:**
```r
result <- some_function(arg1, arg2)
```

**After:**
```r
result <-
  some_function(
    arg1, arg2
  )
```

### Rule 3 — Curly braces (`{` and `}`)

Apply the same logic as Rule 2, but for `{` and `}`:

- Insert a newline **after** every unescaped `{`.
- Insert a newline **before** every unescaped `}`.

**Before:**
```r
if (x > 0) { do_something() }
```

**After:**
```r
if (
  x > 0
) {
  do_something()
}
```

## Scope of transformations

Apply all three rules to **every line** of the file. Do not skip comment lines, string literals, or any other content — apply mechanically unless the delimiter is explicitly escaped with a backslash (`\`).

## Procedure

1. Identify the file to operate on from the `<open_files>` context: use the file marked `active` (currently being edited). Do **not** ask the user which file to use; do **not** operate on any other open file.
2. Use the `read` tool to get the full current content of that file.
3. Apply Rules 1, 2, and 3 to the entire content.
4. Use `write` (with `overwrite: true`) to save the transformed content back to the same file path.
5. Briefly confirm to the user: include the file name and line count before/after.

## Edge cases

- **Chained assignments** (e.g., `a <- b <- value`): apply Rule 1 after each `<-`.
- **Empty parens/braces** (`()`, `{}`): still insert newlines — result is `(\n)` and `{\n}`.
- **Nested delimiters**: apply rules uniformly; indentation may collapse but the flattening is intentional.
- **Escaped delimiters** (`\(`, `\)`, `\{`, `\}`): skip — do not insert newlines around these.
- Do **not** attempt to re-indent the file; only insert newlines as specified.

title: Inline Generate does nothing with Custom Provider (GPT-5.4 family models)
description:
### Environment
- Positron: 2026.06.0-211  
- Posit Assistant: 0.5.10 (build 18d82ef, Jun 3 2026)
- Platform: Windows 10 x64 (NT 10.0.26200), Node.js v22.22.0
- Provider: Custom Provider (openai-compatible)
- Models tested: gpt-5.4-mini, gpt-5.5

### Problem Statement

The inline **Generate** surface (the "Generate" cell button in notebooks) silently 
produces no output when using the Custom Provider with GPT-5.4 family models. Clicking 
Generate, entering a prompt, and submitting results in an empty cell with no error shown 
to the user.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Configure Positron's Custom Provider pointing at an OpenAI-compatible endpoint.
2. Set model to `gpt-5.4-mini` or `gpt-5.5`.
3. Open an R or Python notebook, click **+ Generate**, enter any prompt (e.g. "Write a 
   function to return the first 10 Fibonacci numbers").
4. Observe: no code is inserted into the cell.

### Root Cause (identified via proxy logging)

The Generate surface uses a two-call flow, both with `tools=False`:

**Call 1 — Routing.** Positron asks the model to classify intent and return JSON:

```json
{"participant": "positron.assistant.notebook", "command": "<command>"}
```

The routing system prompt passes an empty `disambiguation` array for both participants:

```json
[{"participant": "setup.notebook", "disambiguation": []},
 {"participant": "positron.assistant.notebook", "disambiguation": []}]
```

With no valid commands listed, the model falls back to the only example in the system 
prompt — which uses `"command": "fix"` as its placeholder. GPT-5.4 Mini returns 
`"command": "fix"` for all requests; GPT-5.5 returns `"command": null`. Neither value 
triggers code insertion in Positron.

**Call 2 — Generation.** The system prompt instructs the model to respond with 
`<replaceString>` XML:

```xml
<replaceString>
<old>text to replace</old>
<new>replacement text</new>
</replaceString>
```

GPT-5.4 Mini returns a plain markdown code block instead. Positron receives the code 
but has no instruction to insert it, so the cell stays empty.

Note: when editing *existing* code via Rewrite → Modify, GPT-5.4 Mini *does* return 
`<replaceSelection>` XML correctly — the issue is specific to fresh generation into an 
empty cell.

### Expected Behaviour

Inline Generate should insert the model's generated code into the notebook cell, 
consistent with the behaviour seen with the built-in Anthropic provider + Claude Sonnet.

### Proposed Fix

Two changes would address the root cause:

1. **Populate `disambiguation`** with the valid command values for each participant so 
   the routing model has actual options rather than guessing from the example placeholder.
2. **Handle plain code block responses** as a fallback in the generation step — if the 
   response contains a fenced code block but no `<replaceString>` tags, treat the code 
   block content as the insertion. This makes the feature robust across models that 
   partially follow the instruction.

---

*The majority of this issue report was drafted by [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/claude-code) 
(Anthropic) following an extended troubleshooting session using a local proxy to inspect 
the full request/response traffic between Positron and the model. The findings, framing, 
and submission have been reviewed and approved by the human submitter.*

title: Compaction settings should use percentages, not absolute token counts
description:
The current compaction configuration (autoCompactTokenBuffer, microCompactTokenThreshold) uses absolute token counts. This is problematic because different models have vastly different context windows (e.g., Claude Sonnet ~200K vs Gemini ~1M).

A fixed autoCompactTokenBuffer: 30000 means very different things:

On a 200K model: triggers at ~85% full (reasonable)
On a 1M model: triggers at ~97% full (hardly any compaction happens before running out of space)
On a 32K model: triggers at ~6% full (compacts almost immediately, unusable)
Proposal: Add percentage-based alternatives, or replace the absolute settings entirely:

{
  "autoCompactTokenBufferPercent": 10,
  "microCompactTokenThresholdPercent": 90
}



These would be computed relative to the model's actual context window size, making them model-agnostic and far more intuitive to configure. A user shouldn't need to know or look up their model's context window size to configure compaction behavior.

The R session can suspend while the user is actively typing in the Posit Assistant chat window. This is disruptive because the user loses their in-progress input or experiences an unexpected interruption. This is only in RStudio Server/Workbench, not Desktop.

Use the `chat/setBusyStatus` notification (or similar mechanism) to signal that the user is currently typing in the chat input, which should prevent session suspension. The busy status should be reset after the user finishes typing (e.g., after a debounced idle period).

Details to be ironed out during implementation.

title: Text output shown in console
description: I've been using Posit Assistant as a teaching assistant to help me learn new concepts in the AI/ML space, and I noticed a UX issue with how it presents explanations. When I ask a conceptual question like "What does X mean?", it answers by calling the `executeCode` tool to `print()` the explanation in the console, rather than just writing the explanation in the chat window. For example, when I asked "What does 20 epochs mean?", it ran the answer through `executeCode` and printed it to the console: Technically, there is nothing wrong with this, but it feels like poor UX. The explanation doesn't need to be executed with `print` statements to be displayed. By comparison, when I ask Claude Code to explain something, it responds with the explanation directly in its window without running anything. That feels more ergonomic and keeps the console reserved for actual code.

title: Import conversation only supports JSON, but no indication is given in the UI
description:
Reported by beta user: https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/issues/17120.

### Description

When using the conversation export/import feature in Posit Assistant 
(accessible via the three-dot menu in the upper-right corner), 
conversations can be exported in three formats: **JSON**, **HTML**, and **Markdown**.

However, only the **JSON** format can be re-imported. Specifically:
- Importing an HTML-exported file silently fails or produces an error.
- The Markdown (.md) format is not even offered as an option in the import dialog.

There is no indication in the UI that JSON is the only supported import format.

### Expected behavior

Either:
1. The UI should clearly indicate that only JSON files can be imported 
   (e.g., a help text or tooltip saying "Only .json files are supported"), 
   or the file picker should be restricted to `.json` files only.
2. Alternatively, import support could be extended to HTML and Markdown formats 
   for consistency with the export options.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Open Posit Assistant in RStudio.
2. Click the three-dot menu (upper-right corner).
3. Export a conversation in HTML or Markdown format.
4. Try to import that exported file using the Import option in the same menu.
5. Observe that HTML import fails and Markdown is not available as an import option.

### Environment

- RStudio version: 2026.04.0-daily+313
- OS: macOS
- Feature: Posit Assistant conversation import/export

### Suggested fix

Add a note or restrict the file picker in the Import dialog to make it 
explicit that only JSON format is supported for import.

title: Regression: Thinking Effort picker now "not available" for ALL Claude models (GitHub Copilot) after update
description:
### What happened

After updating Posit Assistant, the thinking-level (thinking effort) menu now shows **"not available"** for **every** Claude model when using the GitHub Copilot provider — including models where this control worked before the update.

### Why this looks like a regression, not expected behavior

Before the update, the thinking-level menu behaved correctly: it appeared for the Claude models that support adjustable thinking, and stayed hidden for the ones that don't. So Positron was clearly able to tell which models had the feature.

After the update, the menu says "not available" for **all** Claude models — even ones that previously offered it. If this were simply a limitation of the GitHub Copilot route (as suggested in discussion https://github.com/posit-dev/assistant-feedback/discussions/76#discussion-10490966), the behavior would have been consistent all along; it wouldn't have worked before and then stopped for everything at once. Going from "working and correctly detecting which models qualify" to "unavailable for all of them" suggests something broke in the update, rather than this being intended behavior.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Use Claude (e.g. Opus 4.8 or Opus 5) via the **GitHub Copilot** provider.
2. Open the thinking-level / effort menu in the model picker.
3. It shows "not available" for every Claude model.

### Expected behavior

The thinking-level menu should be available for Claude models that support adjustable thinking, as it was before the update.

### Environment

- Posit Assistant: 0.9.1
- Positron: 2026.08.0
- Build / Git Commit: d39be5f (Jul 28, 2026)
- OS: macOS (Darwin 25.5.0), arm64
- Provider: GitHub Copilot (authenticated via the Accounts menu)

### Things I already tried

- "Refresh Models" — *didn't help*
- Full restart of Positron — *didn't  help*

### Related

Discussion https://github.com/posit-dev/assistant-feedback/discussions/76#discussion-10490966 in posit-dev/assistant-feedback describes the same "Thinking level not available" message for Claude Opus 4.8 via GitHub Copilot. That thread frames it as expected for the Copilot route — but the fact that it previously worked and now fails for all models suggests a regression worth investigating.
